title: Fiber Optical Repair Technician
description:
OUR COMPANY:

EOS IT Solutions is a Global Technology and Logistics company, providing Collaboration and Business IT Support services to some of the world’s largest industry leaders, delivering forward-thinking solutions based on multi-domain architecture. Customer satisfaction and commitment to superior quality of service are our top business priorities, along with investing in and supporting our partners and employees.

We are a true International IT provider and are proud to deliver our services through global simplicity with trusted transparency.

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

Role Overview:

The Fiber Optical Repair Technician is responsible for the repair, restoration, and maintenance of fiber optic infrastructure, including splicing, testing, and troubleshooting of both single-mode and ribbon fiber cables. This role ensures the rapid restoration of network services and supports ongoing operational excellence in high-availability environments.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate exceptional technical competency, situational awareness in live network environments, and the ability to lead or coordinate complex restoration efforts under pressure.

Key Responsibilities

Fiber Repair & Restoration

  • Perform fault isolation and repairs on fiber optic cables and connectors, from initial fault detection through to full service restoration.
  • Conduct both emergency restorations and planned maintenance activities with strict adherence to SLAs.
  • Conduct single and ribbon fiber splicing within Meet-Me Vaults (MMVs), splice cases, and central Optical Distribution Frames (ODFs).
  • Perform full cable preparation: jacket stripping, buffer tube access, fiber cleaning, cleaving, splicing, and protection.
  • Use precision tools (fusion splicer, VFL, fiber identifiers) and ensure high-quality workmanship throughout.
  • Adhere to live traffic handling procedures and ensure minimal service disruption during repairs.

Testing & Troubleshooting

  • Operate advanced fiber testing instruments (OTDR, OLTS, power meters, microscopes, and inspection scopes).
  • Conduct post-repair verification, including loss testing, reflectance analysis, and trace review.
  • Accurately interpret OTDR traces and locate break points, microbands, or connector faults.
  • Perform in-depth root cause analysis on recurring or systemic network issues.
  • Implement corrective and preventive measures to improve reliability and reduce fault recurrence.

Documentation & Compliance

  • Maintain accurate records of repair activities, test results, and maintenance logs.
  • Comply with relevant industry standards (ITU-T, FOA, BICSI, TIA/EIA, NEC) and local safety regulations.
  • Support audits and quality assurance processes as required.

Collaboration & Leadership

  • Work closely with field operations, network engineers, and project managers to coordinate repair activities.
  • Provide guidance, mentorship, and on-the-job training to junior team members.
  • Participate in on-call rotations and respond to network outages within defined SLAs (e.g., 4-hour response for emergencies).
  • Communicate clearly with internal teams and clients during critical incidents, providing real-time updates and restoration progress reports.

Continuous Improvement

  • Stay current with the latest fiber optic technologies, repair techniques, and industry best practices.
  • Participate in technical training, cross-functional workshops, and skill enhancement initiatives.
  • Contribute to the refinement of standard operating procedures (SOPs) and restoration workflows.

Required Skills & Experience

Technical Expertise

  • 5+ years’ experience in fiber optic repair, splicing, testing, and restoration — including live-network work.
  • Proficient in using advanced test and repair equipment: OTDR, OLTS, power meter, fusion splicer, fiber identifier, and inspection scopes.
  • Strong ability to interpret OTDR traces, event tables, and loss readings for accurate fault localization.
  • Deep knowledge of fiber types, connector standards (LC, SC, MPO, MTP), and splice protection methods.
  • Experience with both single-mode (OS1/OS2) and multi-mode (OM3/OM4/OM5) fibers.
  • Familiarity with high-count and ribbon fiber systems (864+, 1728+, etc.) and mass fusion techniques.
  • Skilled at working in both OSP (outside plant) and ISP (inside plant) conditions.

Network & Infrastructure Understanding

  • Awareness of data center physical infrastructure, structured cabling systems, and routing standards.
  • Understanding of Layer 1 principles, optical signal flow, and basic network architecture for troubleshooting.
  • Experience restoring and maintaining backbone, metro, or enterprise optical networks.

Diagnostic & Analytical Skills

  • Ability to perform detailed fault isolation under time pressure.
  • Experience conducting root cause analysis and contributing to failure analysis reports.
  • Capable of identifying environmental and mechanical stress factors affecting fiber reliability.

Safety, Quality & Compliance

  • Comprehensive understanding of laser safety, confined space procedures, lockout/tagout (LOTO), and PPE usage.
  • Proven commitment to safety-first practices, maintaining a zero-incident mindset.
  • Demonstrated attention to workmanship quality, cleanliness, and handling of fiber materials.

Soft Skills & Behavioral Attributes

  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making skills under pressure.
  • Clear and professional communication skills for incident coordination and client interaction.
  • Collaborative mindset with the ability to lead or integrate into multidisciplinary field teams.
  • Strong organizational skills, capable of documenting all activities accurately and consistently.
  • Self-motivated, adaptable, and capable of working independently in challenging environments.

Technical Tools & Systems

  • Proficiency with digital reporting systems and fiber management databases.
  • Comfortable using network mapping, GIS, or ticketing platforms for incident tracking.
  • Competent with Microsoft Office Suite, Google Workspace, and documentation software.

Desirable Qualifications

  • Industry certifications such as FOA CFOT, CFOS/T, BICSI Technician, or equivalent.
  • OEM training (e.g., Corning, AFL, or Sumitomo fusion splicer certification).
  • Experience in data center, metro network, or hyperscale infrastructure environments.
  • Prior experience in project leadership, team supervision, or field coordination roles.
  • Valid driver’s license and flexibility to travel or work in variable field conditions.

description:

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.


Department Overview

The Storage and Memory Systems (SMS) Pathfinding team explores future memory and storage technologies that enable next-generation AI, high-performance computing, and data-centric systems. By studying emerging AI workloads, system architectures, and memory technologies, the team helps define innovations that shape the future of computing platforms and memory solutions.

  • Analyze tradeoffs between performance, power, cost, bandwidth, capacity, latency, and scalability across AI systems.
  • Develop models, simulations, benchmarks, and analytical tools to evaluate next-generation memory and storage concepts.
  • Characterize AI workloads running on CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, and memory-centric computing platforms.
  • Collaborate with architects and engineers to assess new technologies, communicate findings, and support proof-of-concept evaluations.

  • 0-2 years of relevant experience through internships, research projects, academic coursework, or technical projects in computer architecture, AI/ML, high-performance computing, or memory systems.
  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
  • Strong understanding of computer architecture, machine learning, artificial intelligence, or high-performance computing concepts.
  • Experience with Python and modern AI/ML frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, or similar technologies.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of memory systems, caching, memory hierarchies, DRAM technologies, and system performance bottlenecks.

title: Senior Product Manager, Access Management
description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.

The Opportunity

Every day, a security administrator somewhere decides who can open which door. A new nurse starts on Monday and needs the medication room but not the server closet. A contractor needs the loading dock for three weeks. Someone leaves the company at 5pm and their badge should stop working at 5:01. Multiply that by 200,000 employees across 400 sites, and you have one of the largest and least-solved logistical problems in enterprise software.

Access control is Verkada's second largest business: hundreds of millions of dollars in sales, growing 40 to 60% year over year, with roughly 80 people building in this area. Access management is the pillar that decides whether all of that feels effortless or exhausting.

We are hiring a Lead Product Manager to own it end to end: users, identities, groups, policies, requests, access levels, and visitor access, from the moment an admin expresses intent to the moment a door opens for the right person.

We do this well today. We think it can be dramatically better, through interfaces that make scale feel simple, APIs and integrations that let the system run itself, and agents that let an admin state what they want instead of clicking through configuration. You will own that as a vertical slice: web and mobile, the backend behind them, the configuration we push to door hardware, and the API and agent surfaces we expose. You will work with a dedicated designer, an engineering manager, and a dedicated engineering team.

We are committed to a thriving in-office culture. This role requires you to work onsite at our HQ in San Mateo, CA.

The access model and administrator interfaces: get the core concepts right

  • Own users, groups, credentials, access levels, door associations, and schedules. This is the conceptual core of the product, and getting it right is the difference between an admin who trusts the system and one who works around it
  • Own the administrative interfaces and experience across web and mobile: bulk operations, search, and review flows that stay fast when a customer has 200,000 users and 10,000 doors
  • Own visitor access, including how guests are invited, credentialed, and expired

Provisioning and integrations: let the system run itself

  • Own the API and integration surface. Most large customers want access to follow their identity provider and HR system automatically, so joiners, movers, and leavers are handled without anyone touching our UI
  • Partner with Verkada's Core team to drive identity integration: SCIM provisioning, SSO, directory sync, and the mapping between an HR record and what a door actually does

Agents and natural language: let admins state intent

  • Define how agents fit into access management. An admin should be able to say what they want and have the system propose the configuration that satisfies it
  • Define the guardrails. Anything that changes who can open a physical door needs review, attribution, and a clean path to undo
  • Build the evaluation framework: accuracy, escalation rate, and how we know a proposed change is safe before it ships to a door

Security posture: surface what looks wrong before it becomes an incident

  • Build the proactive layer: over-provisioned users, credentials that outlived their purpose, access patterns that do not match a door's sensitivity
  • Own audit and compliance reporting, including what a customer hands an auditor to prove who had access to what, and when

Direction

  • Set the direction for access management over multiple years, not just the next few releases, and make the case for it to engineering leadership and the exec team
  • Become the person at Verkada who understands access administrators best. You will define the personas and jobs to be done for this area and make that framework something the rest of the org uses
  • Raise the bar for the product managers around you. You will work alongside four other PMs in access control, and we expect your standards for research, writing, and decision-making to show up in their work too

How You'll Work

  • Own customer discovery. Talk to security administrators directly, go on site walks, and watch someone badge through a building to see where the model breaks down in the real world
  • Set strategy and prioritize the roadmap, balancing reliability, new capability, and the loudest customer in the room
  • Prototype constantly. We expect you to build things to think, not only to write specs about them. You will do this in the interview process too
  • Partner closely with engineering and design, bringing both technical depth and design sense
  • Drive execution from spec to launch with obsessive attention to detail
  • Craft the product pitch with marketing and sales, and help the field sell a capability that is often the reason a deal closes
  • Stay on top of the competitive landscape, the identity ecosystem, and where the market is going
  • Hold several time horizons at once: learning from customers now, planning six and twelve months out, and shipping what launches next quarter

What you'll bring

  • 6+ years of product management experience, currently at Lead or Group-level scope. You have owned a product area, not a single feature, and you set its direction rather than executing someone else's
  • Experience with B2B software used by administrators at scale. with a track record of building and scaling complex enterprise products. Permissions, identity, provisioning, policy, or configuration-heavy admin tooling is directly relevant, as is any product where one person's settings decide what thousands of other people can do
  • A real design partnership. You write problem briefs rather than solutions, you can say why a design is good and not just whether you like it, and you have changed a designer's mind and had yours changed
  • Comfort going deep with engineers on architecture and tradeoffs, then explaining them clearly to customers and executives
  • A standing customer cadence you own, not research handed to you. You can point to a time a customer insight reversed a plan you had already made
  • Explicit prioritization. You can walk through a real sequencing decision: the criteria you used, what you consciously dropped, and who was unhappy about it
  • You enjoy envisioning the big picture and managing the details
  • Strong written and verbal communication. You lead with the recommendation, make the tradeoff explicit, and keep it short enough that people actually read it
  • You like getting your hands dirty and getting out in the field to understand customer pain points

Employee Benefits

Verkada is committed to fostering a workplace environment that prioritizes the holistic health and wellbeing of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive wellness perks, benefits, and resources. Our benefits and perks programs include, but are not limited to:

title: Security Data Engineer
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. Security at that scale runs on data, and you'll be the engineer who owns it and the systems that produce it: component-level hardware inventory and chain of custody, fed by software that runs at our sites and on hosts, and continuous control monitoring, with the posture calculations that decide what each site is cleared to run.

You set the architecture, agree schemas and interfaces with the teams, operators and vendors that own the sources, build the pipelines, stores and tools, and run what you ship. The goal is security that runs itself: custody, access and evidence verified continuously from records, with tools and AI agents doing the reviews. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well.

You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's compute and data center operations teams, and directly with data center operators, hardware vendors and logistics providers. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure.

Key responsibilities

  • Hardware inventory and chain of custody: own the component-level record of what hardware exists, where it is and who has handled it: the data model, the pipelines that join inventory and custody events from many source systems, change history on every record, and the tamper-evident stores behind it

Whether you need to get into a building, drop off a package, ask about store hours or get help in an emergency, the intercom is how you reach a person who can help.

Calling is at the heart of the Intercom experience, and we need a product manager to own it end to end: every call, from the moment someone presses the button to the moment someone answers and helps them.

You'll own the underlying calling pipeline, enterprise-grade call routing, the context and controls that help people answering make better decisions, and the AI that automates call responses. Your job is to make every call reliable, productive and delightful.

Calling stack: make every call great

  • Manage relationships with subprocessors and technology partners, including corporate phone and communications platforms

Call routing: get every call to the best person available

  • Design strategies for concurrent calls: ring strategies (simultaneous, sequential, round robin), triage, queuing, forwarding and failover

We see many more interactions it can automate, including wayfinding, appointment management and granting building entry.

    • Define human escalation rules, clean handoffs and firm guardrails for AI conversations, especially anything safety-related

title: Research Scientist, Life Sciences (Computational Chemistry)
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a research group focused on biological discoveries by combining AI with hands-on biological research. We're seeking a research scientist who combines deep chemistry knowledge with machine learning expertise to join the team. Our goal is to speed up progress in the life sciences by an order of magnitude, and this role puts that mission into practice. You'll be a computational chemist who knows reactions, synthesis, and medicinal chemistry in depth and has hands-on experience training and evaluating machine learning models. Above all, you'll build the reinforcement learning environments, datasets, and evaluations that teach Claude chemistry. Working alongside our bench chemists and AI researchers, you'll turn real chemistry problems and experimental data into training tasks and measure whether the models get better at them.

This role is fully on-site in the San Francisco Bay Area.

Key responsibilities

  • Design and build reinforcement learning environments for chemistry end to end, including task design, data curation, automated grading, and checks against shortcuts and data leakage
  • Design and source new experimental datasets, environments, and evaluations with our bench chemists, and external research and academic partners
  • Develop evaluations that measure model performance on real chemistry tasks, such as reaction outcome prediction, synthesis planning, structure elucidation, and compound design, and feed results back to research teams
  • Run and analyze training experiments with AI research teams, diagnose where models fail at chemistry, and prioritize what to build next
  • Ensure datasets and environments are high quality and well documented, including sources, train and test splits, and failure modes
  • Communicate findings clearly to chemistry, AI research, and life sciences audiences

Minimum qualifications

  • PhD in chemistry, computational chemistry, or a related field
  • Deep knowledge of organic and medicinal chemistry, including reactions, synthesis, and SAR, with experimental data as your ground truth
  • Strong Python skills and solid machine learning fundamentals, with hands-on experience training and evaluating models
  • Comfort navigating ambiguity and defining problems in a rapidly evolving research environment
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams, with strong written and verbal communication skills

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with reinforcement learning, large language models, or building evaluations and benchmarks
  • Track record of supporting drug discovery programs alongside medicinal and synthetic chemists
  • Experience curating chemistry datasets from the literature, patents, or lab notebooks, including reaction, ADMET, and spectroscopic data
  • Cheminformatics and molecular modeling skills, for example RDKit, docking, free energy calculations, or quantum chemistry
  • Hands-on synthetic or medicinal chemistry experience at the bench
  • Publications, patents, or open-source software demonstrating scientific impact

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$300,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Job Summary

The Construction Electrical Manager is responsible for the planning, design, construction, commissioning, and handover of electrical systems for semiconductor manufacturing facilities. The role leads engineers, contractors, consultants, and suppliers to deliver safe, reliable, compliant, and operationally ready electrical infrastructure in accordance with project scope, schedule, cost, quality, and performance requirements.


Key Responsibilities

Electrical Design & Engineering Oversight

· Lead design and engineering of electrical systems for semiconductor manufacturing, cleanroom, and process areas, ensuring capacity, reliability, maintainability, safety, and operational requirements are met.

· Review and approve electrical designs, schematics, wiring diagrams, system layouts, load calculations, short-circuit studies, capacity planning, technical specifications, and other engineering deliverables.

· Lead technical evaluation and selection of electrical equipment, including switchgear, transformers, distribution panels, backup power systems, SMS, and DUPS.

· Lead design, constructability, operability, and technical reviews; resolve electrical design issues and coordinate interfaces with mechanical, structural, and other building and facility systems.

· Evaluate technologies and improvement opportunities that enhance electrical reliability, energy efficiency, sustainability, automation, and lifecycle value.


Construction & Project Execution

· Lead construction and installation of electrical systems in accordance with approved design, safety, quality, cost, and schedule requirements.

· Manage contractors, subcontractors, consultants, and suppliers, including progress, productivity, procurement, equipment delivery, interfaces, field changes, deficiencies, and recovery actions.

· Review and approve electrical submittals, shop drawings, contractor work plans, and installation requirements.

· Develop construction priorities, key milestones, resource plans, shutdown and energization requirements, and mitigation plans to protect critical project and manufacturing milestones.

· Conduct regular site reviews to verify installation quality, workmanship, construction progress, and compliance with approved requirements.

· Manage discipline scope, schedule, cost, risk, procurement, change control, KPIs, and project deliverables; provide clear updates and recommendations to project leadership.


Testing, Commissioning & Handover

· Lead testing, commissioning, energization, startup, functional verification, and operational handover of electrical systems.

· Establish commissioning strategy, acceptance criteria, system turnover sequence, and testing requirements for power distribution, lighting, emergency power, backup power, and associated control systems.

· Coordinate contractors and subcontractors in functional testing, troubleshooting, adjustments, and resolution of commissioning issues to confirm systems meet design and operational requirements.

· Coordinate with Facilities Operations, Maintenance, EHS, manufacturing/end users, contractors, and suppliers to ensure operational readiness and safe transition to operations.

· Ensure complete turnover documentation, including as-built drawings, test reports, operating manuals, equipment records, training documentation, and other required handover information.

· Provide technical leadership during ramp-up and lead root cause analysis and corrective actions for significant electrical system performance or reliability issues.


Safety, Quality & Compliance

· Provide electrical safety leadership and ensure installations, construction activities, testing, commissioning, and energization comply with applicable project safety requirements, electrical codes, and standards.

· Ensure appropriate controls are implemented for electrical installation, energization, live-system interfaces, shutdowns, testing, and other high-risk activities.

· Drive quality controls for electrical equipment, materials, installation, testing, documentation, and system acceptance.

· Promote energy efficiency, sustainability, and electrical safety best practices within semiconductor manufacturing environments.


Stakeholder & Team Leadership

· Act as the primary point of contact for the electrical construction scope, aligning project leadership, project owners, Facilities Operations, manufacturing/end users, EHS, consultants, contractors, subcontractors, and suppliers.

· Lead cross-functional coordination and timely resolution of design, construction, commissioning, and operational interface issues.

· Lead, coach, and develop engineers and project resources; allocate resources according to project priorities and provide technical guidance on complex electrical issues.

· Build effective contractor and supplier partnerships while maintaining clear expectations for safety, quality, schedule, performance, transparency, and accountability.

· Capture lessons learned and drive continuous improvement in electrical designs, construction execution, testing, and commissioning for future projects.


Job Requirements

· Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.

· Minimum 10 years of relevant experience in electrical engineering, facility electrical systems in the semiconductor or high-tech construction industry, including at least 3 years in a supervisory or leadership role

· Strong technical knowledge of electrical power distribution, switchgear, transformers, distribution panels, backup power systems, lighting, control systems, electrical studies, testing, and commissioning.

· Demonstrated construction and project management capability across contractor management, schedule, cost, risk, quality, procurement, interfaces, change control, and system turnover.

· Strong knowledge of applicable electrical codes and standards and strong leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and structured problem-solving skills.


Preferred Qualifications

· Experience delivering large-scale electrical construction and commissioning programs for semiconductor or high-tech manufacturing facilities.

· Proficiency with electrical design and engineering tools such as AutoCAD, Revit, and ETAP.

· Experience attending or supporting factory acceptance testing (FAT) and vendor qualification activities.

· Experience with BIM, digital engineering, data analytics platforms, automation, AI-enabled tools, or other digital solutions that improve engineering, construction, commissioning, operations, or maintenance outcomes.


Working Conditions

This is a site-based role requiring significant presence on the active construction site, together with office-based planning and engineering coordination. Extended hours or weekend support may be required for critical project milestones, shutdowns, energization, testing, and commissioning. Occasional travel may be required for factory acceptance testing (FAT) or vendor qualification activities.

Shape the Future of Semiconductor Innovation

Are you passionate about semiconductor technology, process innovation, and solving complex manufacturing challenges?

title: Creative Designer, Growth
description:
At Evolve, we’re on a mission to make vacation rental easy for everyone. Our high-performing, customer-obsessed team runs on curiosity, communication, and accountability—working together to create exceptional experiences for our owners and guests. Whether solving big challenges, delivering outstanding results, or celebrating wins, we approach every day with purpose and passion. If you’re ready to join a mission-driven company where every teammate has the opportunity to thrive, Evolve might just be the place for you.

Why this role

Evolve is on a mission to make vacation rental easy for everyone, and that starts with the homeowners who trust us with their properties. For most of them, the first thing they see from us is an ad on search or social media, or a referral from another owner. As our Creative Designer, you'll own the strategy behind what we show potential customers across our ads, landing pages and mail pieces. You will work closely with product marketing and our paid marketing teams to test, learn and iterate, and put more of our budget behind what actually brings in qualified owners. This is an individual-contributor role on a small, flat, high-ownership team, with a direct line from your work to the company's growth.

The team

Growth owns Evolve's owner-acquisition funnel, from first impression through qualified lead and signup, and all of our marketing. It's a small team by design, which means less process, more surface area, and a lot of creative freedom inside a clear brand.

What you’ll do

  • Paid Creative
    • Design static, motion and short-form video ads for Meta, Reddit, display and new test channels, with multiple versions of each concept across formats and sizes
    • Ship new variants every week with our performance marketers, built around clear hypotheses — hooks, messages, formats, audiences
    • Read the results with the team, and turn what you learn into the next round rather than starting from scratch
  • Landing Pages, Mail & Brand
    • Design landing page visuals, direct mail pieces and lifecycle email creative, so the experience matches from ad to page to mailbox
    • Work with our brand and product marketing team to keep everything on-brand while still testing boldly
  • Systems & Speed
    • Build templates, asset libraries and a creative learnings log so production scales without losing quality
    • Use AI tools to raise output and speed up iteration, and help the team get better at it

What makes you a great fit

  • 3+ years designing performance or direct-response creative — paid social ads, display, landing pages — for a consumer, marketplace or lead-generation business
  • A portfolio that shows high-volume ad work and how it was tested and iterated, not just final hero pieces
  • Strong in Figma and Adobe Creative Cloud; comfortable with motion and basic video editing (After Effects, Premiere or similar)
  • You think in tests: you can explain why a variant won, and you use performance data to decide what to make next
  • Fast, organized and comfortable with feedback and short turnaround
  • AI-native working style — you already use AI tools to generate, iterate and resize creative; this is a baseline here, not a differentiator
  • Nice to have: experience designing for print or direct mail and working with print vendors, reading Meta Ads Manager or channel dashboards yourself, and copywriting instincts for headlines and hooks

Compensation

Our base salary is $110,000- $135,000 depending on experience.

Location

All Evolve team members must live in one of our approved locations by their first day. We can hire from anywhere in the U.S. except D.C. and Hawaii. Some positions may also have restrictions based on compensation in the following states: California, Maryland, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, and Washington. If you live in Colorado, you can work remotely anywhere in the state, at our downtown Denver office, or a hybrid of both! If you're planning to move soon, please let us know, and we'll be happy to review your application again.

With our core values as our guide, every Evolver helps shape the company we want to work for and the people we want to be. We’ve cultivated a culture of collaboration, care, and responsibility that we can all be proud of, and we’re excited to see what you’ll bring as your authentic self.
